learn.title: Azure Resource Manager, ARM templates and infrastructure as code
objectives: Describe infrastructure as code and why teams use it.
Explain the role of Azure Resource Manager as Azure's deployment and management layer.
Describe the structure and benefits of ARM templates.
Compare ARM template JSON with Bicep, and declarative with imperative approaches.
concepts: Infrastructure as code (IaC)
Defining infrastructure in files that tools deploy, so environments can be versioned, reviewed and recreated consistently.
Declarative
You describe the end state you want, and the tool works out how to reach it. ARM templates and Bicep are declarative.
Imperative
You write the step-by-step commands to run, for example a script of Azure CLI or PowerShell commands.
Azure Resource Manager (ARM)
The deployment and management service for Azure. Requests from the portal, CLI, PowerShell, REST APIs and SDKs all pass through it, and it authenticates and authorises them.
ARM template
A JSON file that declares the resources to deploy. Its main sections are parameters, variables, resources and outputs.
Idempotent
Deploying the same template many times gives the same result; resources already in the declared state are left as they are.
Parameters
Values supplied at deployment time, such as an environment name or VM size, so one template serves many environments.
Outputs
Values returned after a deployment, such as a resource's endpoint.
Bicep
A domain-specific language with simpler syntax than JSON. It compiles to an ARM template, so it supports every Azure resource type.
What-if
A preview of the changes a deployment would make before you run it.
comparisons: ARM is the service that processes every request. An ARM template is a file you give to ARM to describe a deployment.
Both are declarative and produce the same deployments. Bicep is shorter and easier to read, and it compiles to JSON.
Declarative: describe what you want. Imperative: write each step yourself, including handling of what already exists.
Templates are repeatable and versioned. Manual portal steps are error-prone and drift over time.
traps: ARM isn't only for templates. The portal and CLI go through ARM too.
Bicep isn't a separate deployment engine; it compiles to ARM JSON.
Redeploying an ARM template doesn't create duplicate resources.
Terraform is a third-party IaC tool. It isn't an Azure-native template format.
You can export an existing deployment as a template from the portal.
revision: IaC = infrastructure in code files: repeatable, versioned, consistent.
ARM = the management layer for every Azure request, with RBAC, tags, locks and policy applied consistently.
ARM template = declarative JSON with parameters, variables, resources and outputs.
Templates are idempotent, validated before deployment, and deploy resources in parallel where possible.
Bicep = simpler syntax that compiles to ARM JSON.
Declarative describes the end state; imperative describes the steps.
